source_text: 61 DE ZELO CONCUPISCENCIAE. Dum cupis, inde peris, dum ardis proximi zelo; Extinguis te ipsum, quando te incendis abactus. Zelaris alium, inuide, de malo lucrantem, Et te parem concupis fieri pecuniae tantae. Lex sic non aspicit; dum illam incumbere quaeris, Omnia suspensus uiuis in ardore lucrorum; Cumque reus tibi sis ipsum te iudice damnans, Oculorum acies nunquam satiatur auara. Nunc ergo si credeas et cogites: uana cupido est Congere<re> nimium sub fragili uita moranti. Unde Deus clamat: Stulte, hanc noctem uocaris! Postea ruina ruit: cuius erint ista talenta? In suprema cadis iniusta lucra conando, Suggeret cum Dominus unicuique uicta diurna. Congestet alius: tu bono uiuere quaere, Et Deus cor censens agis super omnia uictor; Nec enim dico, ut in timore te mittas, Cum pro die tuo uigilas sine fraude uiuendo. In esca perit auis aut inhaeret inprouida uisco. Arbitrare tibi simpliciter ualde cauendum. Excedant alii, finem tu prospice semper.
pass_a_gloss: Desire/envy → perish. Vain heap under fragili uita. Deus: Stulte, hanc noctem uocaris. Dominus daily victuals. Live bono; Deus weighs heart. Finem tu prospice semper.
pass_b_english: While you desire, from that you perish; while you burn with a neighbor’s envy, you put yourself out when you set yourself on fire, driven. You envy another, envious one, gaining from evil, and you long to become equal to so much money. The law does not look so; while you seek to lean on it, you live suspended in the heat of gains; and while you are guilty to yourself, condemning yourself as judge, the greedy eye’s gaze is never filled. Now therefore if you believe and think: it is vain desire to heap too much under a fragile life that lingers. Whence God cries: “Fool, this night you are called!” Afterward ruin rushes: whose will those talents be? When the Lord supplies each one daily victuals. Let another heap: you seek to live by the good, and God, weighing the heart, you act victor over all things; nor do I say you should cast yourself into fear when you watch for your day living without fraud. A bird perishes in food or sticks unseeing to birdlime. Judge for yourself that you must simply beware hard. Let others go beyond; you always look to the end.

lemmas.sense: Fool, this night you are called
